rules.title: Uses the deprecated Xrm.Page object
rules.fix: Use the form context: take executionContext.getFormContext() in a form handler (pass the execution context as the first parameter), or PrimaryControl in a ribbon command.

rules.title: Uses deprecated Xrm.Utility navigation and dialog methods
rules.fix: Use Xrm.Navigation.openForm, openWebResource, openAlertDialog and openConfirmDialog, and Xrm.Utility.getEntityMetadata for activity checks.

rules.title: Reads the server URL through the deprecated context.getServerUrl
rules.fix: Use Xrm.Utility.getGlobalContext().getClientUrl() (a standalone HTML web resource: ClientGlobalContext.js.aspx, then GetGlobalContext().getClientUrl()). Tool judgment: no Microsoft Learn page names getServerUrl; the sources are the closest statements.

rules.title: Reads a user or organization setting through a global context method that moved
rules.fix: Read the property on Xrm.Utility.getGlobalContext().userSettings (userName, userId, languageId, roles, getTimeZoneOffsetMinutes()) or .organizationSettings (languageId, uniqueName, isAutoSaveEnabled). getUserRoles() returned GUID strings and userSettings.roles holds {id, name} lookups: review each read of the list.

rules.title: Reads a grid row through the deprecated GridRow.getData or GridRowData.getEntity
rules.fix: Use GridRow.data in place of getData() and GridRowData.entity in place of getEntity().

rules.title: Uses the deprecated Xrm.Mobile.offline namespace
rules.fix: Use Xrm.WebApi.offline: the record methods keep their names, and isOfflineEnabled becomes isAvailableOffline.

rules.title: Saves through the deprecated formContext.data.entity.save
rules.fix: Use formContext.data.save, which takes a saveOptions object and runs asynchronously.

rules.title: Uses the deprecated key-press and auto-complete methods
rules.fix: No API replaces these methods: use a custom control built with the Power Apps component framework.

rules.title: Uses the CRM 4.0 crmForm scripting object
rules.fix: Rewrite against the client API: crmForm.all.<attribute>.DataValue becomes formContext.getAttribute("<attribute>").getValue(). crmForm is not part of the documented 9.x client API, and only the documented API is supported. Tool judgment: no Microsoft Learn page names crmForm; the sources are the closest statements.

rules.title: Calls the CRM 4.0 2007 SOAP endpoint
rules.fix: Call the Web API (Xrm.WebApi, or /api/data/v9.x/). The 9.x web services are the Web API, the Organization service and the Organization Data service; the 2007 endpoint is not among them. Tool judgment: no Microsoft Learn page names the 2007 endpoint; the sources are the closest statements.

rules.title: Calls the deprecated CRM 2011 SOAP endpoint
rules.fix: Call the Web API (Xrm.WebApi, or /api/data/v9.x/).

rules.title: Calls the deprecated OData v2 Organization Data Service
rules.fix: Call the Web API (Xrm.WebApi, or /api/data/v9.x/) and drop helper libraries such as SDK.REST.js.

rules.title: Loads the jQuery 2.1.1 the app shipped, removed online in October 2023
rules.fix: Ship the jQuery version the code needs as your own web resource, or remove the dependency.

rules.title: Assembly stored outside the database (on disk or the GAC), which Dataverse online cannot run
rules.fix: Re-register the assembly with its location set to Database (Plug-in Registration Tool, or pac plugin push).

rules.title: Assembly stored outside the database (on disk or the GAC)
rules.fix: Re-register the assembly with its location set to Database, which Microsoft strongly recommends for production plug-ins.

rules.title: Assembly registered without isolation; Dataverse online runs plug-ins only in the sandbox
rules.fix: Re-register the assembly in Sandbox isolation, and check its code against the sandbox limits (no GAC dependencies, HTTP and HTTPS only).

rules.title: Assembly registered without isolation
rules.fix: Consider Sandbox isolation, which a later move to Dataverse online requires; registering an unisolated assembly needs a Deployment Administrator.

rules.title: Plug-in step registered on the System User entity; the on-premises-to-online migration requires none
rules.fix: Unregister the step, or move its logic to a step on another entity or to a process, before the migration. A step whose primary entity is systemuser blocks it.

rules.title: The plug-in project targets .NET Framework below 4.6.2 or references the SDK 5.0 Microsoft.Xrm.Sdk or Microsoft.Crm.Sdk.Proxy assemblies
rules.fix: Retarget the project to .NET Framework 4.6.2 or later (4.8 for the newest platform features) and take Microsoft.Xrm.Sdk and Microsoft.Crm.Sdk.Proxy from the Microsoft.CrmSdk.CoreAssemblies package instead of the SDK 5.0 assemblies. `crm inventory convert --source-map MAP --repo REPO` writes the SDK-style project; the assembly is rebuilt and re-registered afterwards. Judged only for an assembly the source map matches to exactly one project: an unmapped assembly is not read, and an unreadable project is unknown.

rules.title: The plug-in source opens a SQL connection (SqlConnection, SqlCommand or SqlDataAdapter), which the Dataverse online sandbox does not allow
rules.fix: Replace the direct SQL access with Dataverse Web API or IOrganizationService calls (QueryExpression, FetchXML), or move the work to a service the plug-in calls over HTTPS. The online sandbox limits a plug-in to IOrganizationService calls, Azure methods and web access. Detect-only: `crm inventory convert` never rewrites a C# file. Judged only for an assembly the source map matches to exactly one project, from `--source-map` and `--repo`: the project's own C# files are read, a project reached through a ProjectReference is not, and a file that cannot be read or parsed is unknown.

rules.title: The plug-in source reads or writes the file system (File, Directory, FileInfo, DirectoryInfo or FileStream), which the Dataverse online sandbox does not allow
rules.fix: Keep the data in Dataverse (a table, a file or image column, a web resource) or in an Azure service the plug-in calls over HTTPS instead of a local path. Path, Stream and MemoryStream are not file access and are not flagged. Detect-only: `crm inventory convert` never rewrites a C# file. Judged only for an assembly the source map matches to exactly one project, from `--source-map` and `--repo`: the project's own C# files are read, a project reached through a ProjectReference is not, and a file that cannot be read or parsed is unknown.

rules.title: The plug-in source reads or writes the Windows registry (Registry or RegistryKey), which the Dataverse online sandbox does not allow
rules.fix: Move the setting to the step's secure or unsecure configuration, an environment variable, or a configuration table in Dataverse. Detect-only: `crm inventory convert` never rewrites a C# file. Judged only for an assembly the source map matches to exactly one project, from `--source-map` and `--repo`: the project's own C# files are read, a project reached through a ProjectReference is not, and a file that cannot be read or parsed is unknown.

rules.title: An enabled form handler does not pass the execution context to a library that uses Xrm.Page
rules.fix: Select 'Pass execution context as first parameter' on the handler (passExecutionContext="true") and take formContext from executionContext.getFormContext() in the function. Only enabled handlers are judged; a handler whose library cannot be read is unknown, not clear.

rules.title: A form loads a library with an OData v2 call and does not load the OData v2 adapter ahead of it
rules.fix: List the web resource holding the generated OData v2 adapter (crm-odata-v2-adapter.js) in the form's libraries, ahead of the first library that calls the OData v2 endpoint. A library that cannot be read is unknown, not clear.

rules.title: An HTML web resource loads a script with an OData v2 call, or calls the endpoint inline, and does not load the OData v2 adapter ahead of it
rules.fix: Load the web resource holding the generated OData v2 adapter (crm-odata-v2-adapter.js) with a script tag ahead of the first script that calls the OData v2 endpoint, loaded by src or written inline. A page whose script tags or libraries cannot be read is unknown, not clear.

rules.title: A ribbon command calls a library with an OData v2 call and does not load the OData v2 adapter ahead of it
rules.fix: Add an action that calls CrmODataV2.load from the web resource holding the generated OData v2 adapter (crm-odata-v2-adapter.js) ahead of the first action that calls the OData v2 endpoint, in every command that has one. A CustomRule runs at render, before any action, so a rule that calls such a library needs a separate answer. A library that cannot be read is unknown, not clear.

rules.title: A ribbon JavaScriptFunction calls a library that uses Xrm.Page without PrimaryControl among its CrmParameters
rules.fix: Add <CrmParameter Value="PrimaryControl" /> as the first parameter of the action and take the form context from that argument in the function. Only actions on a $webresource: library are judged; one whose library cannot be read is unknown, not clear.

rules.title: Classic dialog (process category 1), deprecated with no automatic conversion
rules.fix: Rebuild the dialog as a business process flow (guided stages on a record) or a canvas app (a scripted or free-form screen); there is no automatic conversion, so redesign it and retire the dialog.

rules.title: Classic workflow with a wait condition, which a cloud flow cannot express
rules.fix: A classic workflow's wait condition (the Postpone activity) has no cloud flow equivalent: Microsoft's Feature capability comparison lists wait conditions on columns as supported by classic workflows only. Microsoft names no replacement pattern, so redesign the process, for example by splitting it at the wait into separately triggered flows. Dataverse online still runs classic workflows, so this is a modernization choice, not a blocker.

rules.title: Classic workflow running a custom workflow activity, which a cloud flow cannot run
rules.fix: A classic workflow's custom workflow activity (an ActivityReference to an assembly other than Microsoft.Crm.Workflow) has no cloud flow equivalent: Microsoft's Feature capability comparison lists running custom background workflow activities as supported by classic workflows only. Microsoft documents running Dataverse actions, including custom actions, from a flow, so move the activity's logic into a custom action or plug-in and call it from the flow. Dataverse online still runs classic workflows, so this is a modernization choice, not a blocker.

rules.title: Custom SQL-based report: Dataverse online runs Fetch-based reports, and the migration removes custom SQL-based reports that were not converted
rules.fix: Rewrite the report's datasets in FetchXML and switch its data source to the Fetch data provider (MSCRMFETCH). Microsoft documents no converter. A rewritten report must still pass the Dataverse RDL sandbox, so a Fetch rewrite is not proof that it runs. The migration removes a custom SQL-based report that was not converted.

rules.title: A script or HTML web resource names the source org's host, which the migration switches off
rules.fix: After the upgrade the source server is switched off, so this text points at a host that no longer answers. Replace the absolute address with a relative one, or with the current org URL read at run time (Xrm.Utility.getGlobalContext().getClientUrl() in script). The match is on the host name the run was given, so a comment naming it is reported too.
